name: 16c tensor parallel mlp
title: Tensor-parallel MLP on two GPUs
subtitle: x = (1, 2). GPU 1 owns columns 1 and 2 of the first matrix and rows 1 and 2 of the second; GPU 2 owns columns and rows 3 and 4

steps.caption: Both GPUs start with the same input x = (1, 2). GPU 1 holds columns (1, 0) and (0, 1) of the first matrix, GPU 2 holds columns (1, -1) and (-1, 1).
Each GPU multiplies x by its own two columns with no communication: GPU 1 gets hidden units (1, 2) and GPU 2 gets (-1, 1).
ReLU acts on each hidden unit separately, so each GPU applies it locally: (1, 2) stays (1, 2) and (-1, 1) becomes (0, 1).
Each GPU multiplies its two hidden units by its two rows of the second matrix. GPU 1 gets the partial output (1, 2) and GPU 2 gets (2, -1).
One all-reduce adds the partials: (1, 2) + (2, -1) = (3, 1) on both GPUs, exactly the output of the unsplit MLP.
Splitting the first matrix by rows would leave each GPU with partial sums of the pre-activations. ReLU of each partial then added gives (1, 2, 1, 2), but the correct hidden layer is (1, 2, 0, 1).
